questions.question: A magnetic field is a region in which a magnetic force is experienced by a
questions.explanation: A magnetic field exerts a force only on a moving charge. A stationary charge does not experience a magnetic force.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of magnetic flux density is the
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density (B) is measured in tesla (T). One tesla is one weber per square metre.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of magnetic flux is the
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux (Φ) is measured in weber (Wb). One weber is one tesla square metre.

questions.question: One tesla is equivalent to
questions.explanation: B = Φ/A, so 1 T = 1 Wb m<sup>-2</sup>.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines outside a magnet run from the
options: South pole to the north pole
North pole to the south pole
questions.explanation: Outside a magnet, field lines run from the north pole to the south pole.

questions.question: The magnetic field lines inside a magnet run from the
options: North pole to the south pole
South pole to the north pole
questions.explanation: Inside a magnet, field lines run from the south pole to the north pole, completing the loop.

questions.question: Magnetic field lines
options: Always start from the south pole
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines never intersect because at any point the field has a unique direction.

questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field at a point is the direction in which the north pole of a
questions.explanation: The direction of B is the direction a free compass needle would point (north pole).

questions.question: The magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying conductor at a distance r from it is
questions.explanation: B = μ0I/(2πr), so B is inversely proportional to r.

questions.question: The magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying conductor is directly proportional to the
questions.explanation: B = μ0I/(2πr), so B is directly proportional to current I.

questions.question: The magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying conductor forms
questions.explanation: The field lines form concentric circles around the conductor.

questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor is given by
questions.explanation: The right-hand grip rule (Maxwell's screw rule) gives the direction of B around a current-carrying conductor.

questions.question: The magnitude of the force on a charge q moving with velocity v in a magnetic field B at an angle θ is
questions.explanation: F = qvB sinθ, where θ is the angle between v and B.

questions.question: The magnetic force on a charged particle is zero when the particle moves
questions.explanation: When the particle moves parallel to the field, θ = 0° or 180°, so sinθ = 0 and F = 0.

questions.question: The magnetic force on a charged particle is maximum when the particle moves
questions.explanation: F = qvB sinθ is maximum when θ = 90°, i.e., perpendicular to the field.

questions.question: A proton of charge 1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup>C moves with a velocity of 1.0 × 10<sup>6</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup> through a magnetic field of 1.0T at an angle of 30°. The force on the proton is
The force on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field is always
options: Perpendicular to both the velocity and the field
Perpendicular to the velocity but parallel to the field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force F = q(v × B) is perpendicular to both v and B.

questions.question: The path of a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field is
questions.explanation: When v is perpendicular to B, the force is perpendicular to v, causing circular motion.

questions.question: The radius of the circular path of a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: Equating magnetic force to centripetal force: qvB = mv2/r ⇒ r = mv/(qB).

questions.question: An electron moving perpendicular to a magnetic field of flux density 0.5T has a speed of 2.0 × 10<sup>6</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup>. If the mass of the electron is 9.1 × 10<sup>-31</sup>kg and its charge is 1.6 × 10<sup>-19</sup>C, the radius of its path is approximately
A charged particle is projected into a magnetic field. If the particle moves parallel to the field, its path will be
questions.explanation: If v is parallel to B, the magnetic force is zero, so the particle moves in a straight line.

questions.question: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: F = BIL sinθ, where θ is the angle between the conductor and the magnetic field.

questions.question: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is maximum when the conductor is
questions.explanation: F = BIL sinθ is maximum when θ = 90°, i.e., perpendicular to the field.

questions.question: A conductor of length 0.5m carrying a current of 2A is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of flux density 0.4T. The force on the conductor is
The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

questions.question: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb, the forefinger and the middle finger held mutually at right angles represent respectively
questions.explanation: In Fleming's left-hand rule: thumb = motion, forefinger = field, middle finger = current.

questions.question: The device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy using the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is the
questions.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.

questions.question: The magnetic field inside a solenoid carrying current is
questions.explanation: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform (constant in magnitude and direction).

questions.question: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is directly proportional to the
options: Current and number of turns per unit length
questions.explanation: B = μ0nI, so B is proportional to current I and turns per unit length n.

questions.question: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is given by
questions.explanation: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is B = μ0nI.

questions.question: The relative permeability of a ferromagnetic material is
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials have relative permeability much greater than 1 (e.g., iron ≈ 1000).

questions.question: The relative permeability of a diamagnetic material is
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have relative permeability slightly less than 1.

questions.question: A material that is strongly attracted by a magnet is said to be
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted by magnets.

questions.question: Which of the following is a ferromagnetic material?
questions.explanation: Iron is a ferromagnetic material. Copper and bismuth are diamagnetic; aluminium is paramagnetic.

questions.question: Which of the following is a diamagnetic material?
questions.explanation: Bismuth is diamagnetic. Iron, nickel, and cobalt are ferromagnetic.

questions.question: The angle of dip at the magnetic equator is
questions.explanation: At the magnetic equator, the earth's field is horizontal, so the angle of dip is 0°.

questions.question: The angle of dip at the magnetic poles is
questions.explanation: At the magnetic poles, the earth's field is vertical, so the angle of dip is 90°.

questions.question: The angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian at a place is called the angle of
questions.explanation: The angle between magnetic and geographic meridians is the angle of declination.

questions.question: The angle between the direction of the earth's magnetic field and the horizontal at a place is called the angle of
questions.explanation: The angle between the earth's field and the horizontal is the angle of dip (inclination).

questions.question: The horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: If δ is the angle of dip, horizontal component BH = B cosδ.

questions.question: The vertical component of the earth's magnetic field is given by
questions.explanation: Vertical component BV = B sinδ.

questions.question: The neutral point in a magnetic field is a point where the resultant magnetic field is
questions.explanation: At a neutral point, the resultant magnetic field is zero.

questions.question: The instrument used to detect the presence of a magnetic field and its direction is the
questions.explanation: A compass needle detects the presence and direction of a magnetic field.

questions.question: A short bar magnet placed in the earth's magnetic field with its north pole pointing north will have
options: Two neutral points on the east and west sides
Two neutral points on the north and south sides
questions.explanation: With the north pole pointing north, neutral points lie on the east and west sides (equatorial line).

questions.question: Magnetic flux is measured in
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux is measured in weber (Wb).

questions.question: Magnetic flux density is defined as the magnetic flux per unit
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux density B = Φ/A, where A is the area perpendicular to the field.

questions.question: A soft iron rod placed inside a solenoid increases the magnetic field because soft iron has
questions.explanation: Soft iron has high permeability, which concentrates the magnetic field lines and increases B.

questions.question: The core of an electromagnet is usually made of soft iron because soft iron
options: Retains magnetism for a long time
Becomes magnetized easily and loses its magnetism easily
Is a good conductor of heat
questions.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetized and demagnetized, making it ideal for electromagnets.

questions.question: Steel is preferred to soft iron in making permanent magnets because steel
options: Retains its magnetism for a long time
questions.explanation: Steel has high retentivity, so it retains magnetism for a long time.

questions.question: The magnetic force between two parallel current-carrying conductors carrying currents in the same direction is
questions.explanation: Currents in the same direction attract each other; currents in opposite directions repel.
